items.title: Robot Hand Achieves Ancient Embroidery Mastery
points: AGILINK's OmniHand 3 Ultra splits individual silk threads into 16 strands, threads needles, stretches fabric, and executes stitches with force adjustment as materials bend—a process refined by humans over 2,500 years.
The robot features 21 active degrees of freedom (joint positions it can control independently), allowing it to adapt as slippery thread shifts during work.

Reinforcement learning (machine learning where the system improves by trial and error) enables the robot to handle material properties that vary unpredictably—a major step toward human-like manual dexterity.

items.title: California Halts Unregulated Human-Robot Combat
points: YouTuber Frankie LaPenna fought three humanoid robots in an unsanctioned San Francisco event that generated viral social media views.
California's athletic commission issued a cease-and-desist order to robotics company REK, stating any martial arts exhibition involving a human requires a valid promoter's license.
The regulatory response signals that authorities will treat robot combat exhibits like traditional fighting sports when human safety is involved, requiring formal oversight and licensing.

items.title: Humanoid Robotics Investment and Deployment Growth
points: Nvidia is reportedly considering a fresh $1B investment in Figure AI; the chipmaker already backed Figure's $1B Series C round in 2025 that valued the startup at $39B.
Nvidia supplies technology powering Figure's Helix robot models, and a new investment would deepen the company's strategy of backing hardware users rather than solely selling chips.
FireFly Robotics filed for a Nasdaq direct listing under ticker 'FFLY,' signaling public market confidence in autonomous turf-care robotics as revenue scales.

items.title: New Robot Systems Enter Dangerous Work Environments
points: Minerva Humanoids unveiled Roger, a walking robot built in 5 months that uses teleoperation (remote control via VR headset worn by a human operator) for hazmat and bomb disposal tasks.
Onboard software handles balance, navigation, and fall recovery autonomously while the human controls the robot's hands and movement strategy through VR camera feeds.

A new report details powered exoskeletons now being deployed by Seattle rescue teams, warehouse staff, auto workers, and soldiers in combat zones, with falling component costs making the technology economically viable.
Meteomatics' reusable stratospheric drone reached 34,245 feet, surpassing commercial aircraft altitude to gather weather data traditionally collected by weather balloons.
